title: SB 467: SCC grid-impact finding before local permits for 90 MW+ facilities
summary: Localities cannot issue zoning, building or erosion permits for 90 MW+ facilities until the SCC finds no or minimal grid impact.
status_detail: Carried over to 2027 · Senate Commerce & Labor, 11-4, 2/9/26

title: SB 619 / HB 155: SCC certificate required to operate high-load facilities
summary: No new facility over 90 MW (25 MW in HB 155) may operate without an SCC certificate finding no material harm to rates, reliability or clean-energy compliance.
status_detail: Failed – vote · SB 619 passed Senate 23-16, then tabled 9-0 in a House subcommittee 3/3/26; HB 155 tabled 9-0

title: HB 507: Tier 4 emission limits for data center backup generators
summary: DEQ may not issue air permits for data center applications filed on or after 7/1/26 unless every generator meets Tier 4-equivalent limits.
status_detail: Enacted · Ch. 397, signed 4/8/26, effective 7/1/26

title: HB 1333: By-right development on poor-soil farmland; host payments from data centers
summary: Projects on poor-soil agricultural land become by-right uses, overriding local zoning; data centers with new tax awards pay 1% of exempted tax to the host unit.
status_detail: Failed – adjournment · Passed House 54-45 (both sources); died in Senate Utilities

title: HB 2456: Nuclear-ready communities; county land for large electricity users
summary: County comprehensive plans must designate land for very large electricity users, including data centers, and plan for small modular reactors.
status_detail: Failed – vote · Passed Senate 16-12; House final vote failed 28-27-5 (31 needed), 6/9/26

title: HB 2452: County plans may not prevent data centers
summary: Large counties must designate enough land that plans "not prevent or prohibit" data centers; update within 2 years.
status_detail: Failed – vote · House third reading 25-29-6, 2/25/26

title: HB 4009: State trust land map for data centers and power plants
summary: State Land Department maps the best state-trust parcels for data centers and power plants every 10 years.
status_detail: Failed – vote · House third reading 29-25-6 (31 needed), 2/26/26

title: HB 646: Self-supply, separate tariff and disclosure rules for data centers
summary: Current Senate substitute (data centers over 25 MW): new data centers over 250 MW must supply their own power or offset grid use, data center service costs go only to data centers under a separate tariff, local property-tax abatements capped at 50%, water metering and reporting, wastewater monitoring, and NDAs cannot block public records. No longer creates a study commission.
status_detail: Pending – passed one chamber · Passed House (amended) 2026-03-18; Senate Energy reported substitute 2026-06-10, informally passed, then recommitted to Senate Energy the same day. Vote counts not shown in packet.

title: HB 710: Ban on incentives and on building new data centers on farmland
summary: For new data centers (construction not started, no final local approval): bans all state and local incentives with refund; bars construction on prime farmland (unless voluntarily sold and county commissioners approve), public land, or platted residential neighborhoods; bars eminent domain for them; requires PUCO ratepayer-neutrality finding before approval or interconnection.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-02-24; referred to House General Government 2026-02-25.

title: HB 983: Local vote and off-grid power required for new data centers
summary: Data Center Accountability and Citizen Protection Act (emergency clause): local citizen vote required for any new or expanded data center within 5 miles; voter-approved centers must self-generate 100% of power off-grid with closed-loop cooling; strict air/wastewater limits with permit revocation; bans local tax incentives.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-07-28; no further action.

title: SB 378: State permit and 5 MGD cap on data center water use
summary: Responsible Water Use by Data Centers Act: requires a state consumptive-use permit for any data center water withdrawal, caps new or increased consumptive use at 5 million gallons per day, and makes data centers pay water/sewer infrastructure costs.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-03-16; referred to Senate Public Utilities 2026-03-25.

title: SB 381: PUCO approval before data centers can seek grid interconnection
summary: Ohio Power Responsibility and Fairness Act: no one may apply for grid interconnection for a data center (over 25,000 kWh demand, incl. crypto) without prior PUCO approval after an independent 270-day grid-impact forecast paid by applicant; PUCO may deny, bar interconnection, and must also approve the agreement.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-03-19; referred to Senate Public Utilities 2026-03-25.

title: HB 392: Right to Compute Act limits local restrictions
summary: Ohio Right to Compute Act: bars any political subdivision or state agency from restricting lawful use or development of computational resources (including infrastructure) unless narrowly tailored to a compelling governmental interest; also requires AI risk-management policies for AI-controlled critical infrastructure.
status_detail: Pending – reported from committee · Introduced 2025-07-07; reported as amended by House Technology and Innovation 2026-06-10. No floor vote shown.

title: HB 1834 / SB 1323: Data Center Act: clean firm power and large-load rules
summary: Data Center Act: for commercial data centers (25 MW+), PUC large-load rules with clean firm energy requirements (with alternative compliance payments), disclosure, backup generation and curtailment standards, plus cost-shifting bans and LIHEAP contributions.
status_detail: Pending – passed one chamber · House passed 104-95 on 2026-03-24 (as amended); in Senate, referred to Consumer Protection & Professional Licensure 2026-03-31.

title: HB 2151: State model zoning ordinance for data centers
summary: Directs state Local Government Commission to publish a model zoning ordinance for data centers (setbacks, buffers, dimensional standards, community benefit agreements) and give technical assistance; municipalities not required to adopt it.
status_detail: Pending – passed one chamber · House passed 124-77 on 2026-04-13; in Senate, referred to Local Government 2026-04-23.

title: HB 2246: DEP water review for data centers using 100,000+ gal/day
summary: For data centers consuming over 100,000 gal/day (30-day), DEP gets preapplication notification, added Clean Streams permit conditions, aquifer tests, river basin commission approval, must deny where adverse water impact is foreseeable, and can force withdrawal to cease.
status_detail: Pending – passed one chamber · House passed 116-84 on 2026-04-27; in Senate, referred to Environmental Resources & Energy 2026-05-01.

title: HB 2516: Zoning standards and 2,500 ft setbacks for data centers
summary: Amends Municipalities Planning Code for commercial data centers (25 MW+): zoning must expressly authorize them with standards, minimum 2,500 ft setback from residences and 300 ft from roads, ban in agricultural security areas and conservation easements, mailed notice within one mile, and municipal power to prohibit in all districts.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to House Local Government 2026-05-13; no further action.

title: HB 2821: Local voter approval for high-impact data centers
summary: Local option: a municipal plat approval for a high impact data center (25 MW+) is not final until voters approve it at the next election at least 100 days later; a majority no vote denies the application.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to House Local Government 2026-10-02; no further action.

title: SB 991: Preapproved sites and fast-track DEP permitting
summary: Data Center Siting and Permitting Act: DEP lists at least 15 preapproved sites (5 at retiring power plants), offers two-phase accelerated permitting with 3-day notices to proceed, certified-professional submissions, prevailing wage condition, and tolls permit timelines during litigation.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to Senate Environmental Resources & Energy 2025-09-05; no further action.

title: SB 1460: Data centers barred from residential zones
summary: Municipalities Planning Code amendment: no data center may be established or operated in a residential zoning area, and hyperscale/major data centers (5,000+ servers and 100,000+ sq ft) may only be located in an industrial and mining zone.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to Senate Local Government 2026-09-24; no further action.

title: SB 724: Data Center Fair Share Act: LIHEAP payments and renewable supply
summary: Data Center Fair Share Act (25 MW+ large load customers): $10,000/MW annual LIHEAP payments, 25% incremental renewable supply requirement, community benefits agreement with at least 10% of project cost, cost-allocation rules, and prohibition on contract confidentiality terms.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to Senate Consumer Protection & Professional Licensure 2026-03-31; no further action.

title: HB 2588: Limits on hyperscale data centers on farmland
summary: Zoning may not allow hyperscale data centers (over 5 acres, 10 MW+) in districts where farming is permitted unless no other district allows them, and may not allow any 10 MW+ data center on a farm-district tract that is at least 50% prime farmland or class 4 soils.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to House Local Government 2026-06-02; no further action.

title: HB 1764: Regional-impact review for large developments
summary: Creates a regional-impact review under the Planning Code: land developments including data centers (25 MW+) need an impact analysis, mitigation plan and hearing, and the host municipality may approve, condition or disapprove; applicant pays all costs and review clocks are extended.
status_detail: Pending – reported from committee · Referred to House Local Government 2025-07-24; reported as amended and laid on the table 2025-12-17 (procedural); no floor vote.

title: A 1170 / S 680: New clean power and BPU-approved energy plan for AI data centers
summary: Contingent on BPU finding that a majority of PJM states impose similar rules, AI data centers must source all power from new Class I renewable or nuclear and get BPU approval (90-day review) of an energy usage plan before connecting to the grid. S 680 also covers crypto mining.
status_detail: Pending – reported from committee · Reported from Senate Environment and Energy Committee 2026-03-16; referred to Senate Budget and Appropriations
threshold: AI data centers (no MW threshold in text)

title: A 4769 / A 5729 / S 3639: Expedited permits for data centers with on-site power
summary: Requires BPU, DCA and DEP to adopt rules within 12 months for expedited approval and permitting of AI data centers with their own power: on-site small modular reactors (A 4769 / S 3639) or on-site natural-gas generation (A 5729), including model expedited local approvals.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-03-19; referred to Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee

title: A 5294 / S 4402: State Planning Commission review of large-load data centers
summary: Statewide framework for large load data centers (peak load 25 MW or more): State Planning Commission must approve a resource impact statement (60 days, deemed approved if silent) before municipalities may approve site plans or subdivisions; DEP permit needed for diversions over 100,000 gallons/day.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-18; referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee

title: A 5622 / S 4657: Environmental justice review for data center permits
summary: Amends the Environmental Justice Law: one year after enactment, DEP will not deem a permit application for a new data center (over 1 MW annual demand) complete without an environmental justice impact statement and public hearing, and can deny the permit for disproportionate cumulative impact, even outside overburdened communities.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-10-15; referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee

title: S 3611: State Planning Commission approval of data center site plans
summary: Planning boards must send data center site plan and major subdivision applications to the State Planning Commission and BPU, and cannot grant final approval without SPC approval (45 days, deemed approved if silent); data centers made ineligible for economic development subsidies.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-02-19; referred to Senate Community and Urban Affairs Committee

title: Budget (HB 30): $0.011/kWh tax on data center electricity use
summary: Budget (HB 30) adds a $0.011/kWh tax on all electricity used at covered data centers, utility-supplied or self-generated, capped at $600M a year with any excess refunded; the sales-tax exemption is kept and data center tax policy is to be reviewed.
status_detail: Enacted in HB 30 (signed Jun 30, 2026)

title: SB 410: Repeal of the data center sales tax exemption
summary: Repealed the data center sales tax exemption; passed the Senate, died in House Ways & Means.
status_detail: Failed – adjournment

title: HB 1210: Data centers pay host localities part of exempted tax
summary: Data centers with post-6/30/26 tax awards pay up to 1% of exempted electricity tax to the host locality.
status_detail: Enacted (PL 157)

title: HB 4168: Pause on new data center tax-relief certifications
summary: Pauses new data center tax-relief certifications 7/1/26–6/30/29.
status_detail: Enacted (Ch. 140)

title: SB 6 (2025): Large-load interconnection, cost sharing and curtailment
summary: Large-load law (75 MW+): interconnection standards, cost sharing, curtailment and backup-power switching in emergencies.
status_detail: Enacted 6/20/25

title: HB 2198: Repeal of the data center equipment tax incentive
summary: Repeals the data center equipment tax incentive program; in Senate Finance.
status_detail: Pending – passed House

title: S 4390 / A 5165: End Data Center Tax Credits Act
summary: End Data Center Tax Credits Act: takes up to $250M of Next New Jersey tax credits away from AI data center projects and redirects them, including up to $125M for energy storage projects.
status_detail: Enacted (P.L.2026, c.77)

title: A 796 / S 731: Utility rate rules so data centers pay their own costs
summary: Special utility rate rules so data centers pay their own costs.
status_detail: Enacted (P.L.2026, c.32)

title: HB 957 / SB 374 / HB 999: No new data center tax exemptions
summary: Would bar new data center sales and property tax exemptions.
status_detail: Pending – in committee

title: Governor's directive: ERCOT audit and pause of data center queue
summary: PUCT and ERCOT ordered to audit every data center in ERCOT's interconnection queue and pause their advancement until the audit is done.
status_detail: In effect

title: Governor's directive: data centers pay their own grid costs
summary: Letter directing the PUCT to make data centers pay their own grid infrastructure costs; Abbott plans to codify this and end data center incentives in 2027.
status_detail: Agency response due July 17, 2026

title: Executive Order 2026-05: GRID standards for data centers
summary: Official text, for data centers over 25 MW: developers who sign a GRID consent order get rolling DEP review, but permits issue only after all local zoning approvals; developers who do not sign get no DEP review until they have all local and water approvals, no rolling issuance and no permit-decision guarantee. GRID compliance also required for the sales-tax exemption; data centers removed from Permit Fast Track; state NDAs banned; public project map.
status_detail: In effect for permits filed after Aug 18, 2026

title: Governor's directive: pause on new data center tax exemptions
summary: Gov. DeWine directed the Ohio Tax Credit Authority to stop considering new data center sales-tax exemption requests while the Joint Data Center Committee studies the industry.
status_detail: Announced; current status unconfirmed

title: HB 5513: Hyperscale data center limits near equity and EJ communities
summary: Bars building or expanding a data center within 3 miles of equity-investment-eligible or Chicago EJ communities unless the EPA completes an applicant-funded cumulative impact assessment, and adds Water Impact Permits, generator limits, community benefits agreements and an NDA ban.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Re-referred to Rules Committee under Rule 19(a) on 2026-03-27; no later action through 2026-09-30 other than co-sponsor additions.

title: HB 5755: Hearing and voter referendum on data center siting
summary: Requires a municipal public hearing within 60 days and makes any data center siting approval (5 MW or more, or qualifying Illinois data centers) subject to a back-door referendum on a petition of 15% of votes cast; a No vote bars approval.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to Rules Committee on 2026-05-05; no further action.
threshold: 5 MW+ connected load, or any qualifying Illinois data center

title: SB 4206: Local siting authority and 3-mile consent rule
summary: Lets counties and municipalities set data center siting, size, water and noise standards, bars siting within 3 miles of another municipality without its written consent, and requires a public hearing within 30 days before the siting decision.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to Assignments on 2026-05-18; no further action.

title: HB 5396: Repeal data center sales tax exemption
summary: Repeals the sales tax exemption for data center equipment (section 4ee) and removes related school aid fund provisions.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced and referred to Economic Competitiveness Committee 2025-12-17; no further action.

title: HB 5398: Property tax conforming bill for exemption repeals
summary: Conforming amendment to the general property tax act (sec. 7ff) to reflect repeal of data center tax exemptions; takes effect only if HB5396 and HB5397 are enacted.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2025-12-17; referred to Economic Competitiveness; no further action

title: HB 5777: Registration and financial security for 5 MW+ data centers
summary: Requires large-scale data centers (5 MW or 25,000 sq ft) to register with EGLE, pay fees, and post financial security for decommissioning and cleanup before operating; director may suspend or revoke; annual energy and water reports.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-04-14; referred to Government Operations; no further action
threshold: 5 MW critical IT load or 25,000 sq ft

title: HB 6136: Zoning law made subject to community benefit agreements
summary: Makes local zoning ordinances subject to the data center community benefit agreement act (HB6137); effective only if HB6137 is enacted.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-25; no further action

title: HB 6137: Community benefit agreements required for data centers
summary: No data center construction or operation without a community benefit agreement approved by the locality and the PSC (90-day decisions); localities and PSC may not approve permits or interconnection without it.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-25; no further action

title: HB 6388: Zoning law made subject to data center siting act
summary: Amends Michigan zoning enabling act sec. 205 so zoning ordinances are subject to the data center siting and community protection act (HB6391); takes effect only if HB6391 is enacted.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-09-24; referred to Government Operations; no further action through 2026-09-30.

title: HB 6391: Local site certificates for 25 MW+ data centers
summary: Large-scale data centers (25 MW IT or 50 MW total) need a local site certificate backed by acoustic, agricultural, thermal and cumulative impact assessments, no-feasible-alternative showing for farmland or wetlands, no-material-adverse-effect findings and a monitoring agreement.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-09-24; referred to Government Operations; no further action through 2026-09-30.
threshold: 25 MW IT load or 50 MW total demand

title: SB 1019: Zoning law made subject to data center moratorium act
summary: Amends Michigan zoning enabling act sec. 205 so zoning ordinances are subject to the data center regulation act (the SB1018 moratorium to April 1, 2027); takes effect only if SB1018 is enacted.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-04; referred to Government Operations; no further action through 2026-09-30.

title: SB 1050: Local community benefit agreements required for data centers
summary: No data center may begin construction or operation without a local government-approved community benefit agreement; the locality must approve or deny within 90 days and may deny permits where none is approved.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-18; referred to Energy and Environment; co-sponsors added; no committee action through 2026-09-30.

title: SB 1051: Zoning law made subject to community benefit act
summary: Amends Michigan zoning enabling act sec. 205 so zoning ordinances are subject to the data center community benefit act (SB1050); takes effect only if SB1050 is enacted.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-18; referred to Energy and Environment; co-sponsors added; no committee action through 2026-09-30.

title: HB 399: Shorter data center tax abatements and purchase taxes
summary: Limits data processing center tax abatements to 20 years for abatements granted from 2027 (30 with a local investment agreement), requires sales and ad valorem tax on certain large data center purchases, and extends the abatement sunset.
status_detail: Enacted · House passed 102-0 (2026-03-10); Senate passed as amended 32-0 (2026-04-09); House concurred 102-0 (2026-04-09); enacted 2026-04-17.

title: SB 270: PSC public-interest test for 150 MW+ data center contracts
summary: Directs the PSC, when reviewing contracts for 150 MW or larger data center loads, to find them in the public interest only if they recover incremental costs and benefit other customers; effective 2026-10-01.
status_detail: Enacted · Senate passed 30-0 (2026-03-12); House passed as amended 100-1 (2026-04-08); Senate concurred 33-0 (2026-04-08); enacted 2026-04-17.

title: SB 102: 100% renewable and cost rules for 30 MW+ data centers
summary: For data centers over 30 MW (or 60 MW collectively), requires 100% renewable power from 2031 plus hourly matching, 15-year cost contracts, site assessments, cumulative impact analysis and community benefit agreements, water and backup generator rules, and bars utility interconnection otherwise.
status_detail: Failed – vote · Senate Transportation & Energy postponed indefinitely 9-0 on 2026-05-11.

title: HB 4084: Enterprise zone tax break limits for data centers
summary: Economic development package with fast-track permitting council; bars enterprise zone property tax exemption extensions for data centers and blocks authorizing data center projects in enterprise zones until 90 days after the 2027 session adjourns (repealed 2029-01-02).
status_detail: Enacted · Governor signed 2026-03-31; Chapter 50 (2026 Laws), effective June 5, 2026; House 50-5 (2026-03-04), Senate 21-8 (2026-03-06)

title: HB 4509: Restore local control over high impact data centers
summary: Restores county and municipal jurisdiction over certified microgrid districts and high impact data centers by removing the state preemption of local zoning, permitting and licensing in WV Code 5B-2-21b.
status_detail: Failed – adjournment · Introduced and referred to House Energy and Public Works 2026-01-19; no further action

title: HB 4983: Commerce rule for high impact data center certification
summary: Authorizes the Commerce Department legislative rule (145 CSR 20) on certification of microgrid districts and high impact data centers, with an amendment adding 'or access of water' to section 2.4.
status_detail: Enacted · Approved by Governor 2026-03-27 (recorded 2026-03-30); House 78-16 (2026-02-17), Senate 28-6 (2026-03-11), House concurred 82-15 (2026-03-13)
